summary: Catharine Bird Runkle was an Indologist. She studied at Radcliffe College in 1886 under Charles Rockwell Lanman.

Catherine Bell was a scholar of religious studies and Sinology. She studied at the University of Chicago under Joseph M. Kitagawa (~1976–1983) and served as Bernard J. Hanley Professor of Religious Studies at Santa Clara University (1985–2008).

Catherine Cornille works in religious and Buddhist studies. She earned degrees at KU Leuven and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. She held posts at KU Leuven, College of the Holy Cross, and Boston College, becoming Associate Professor in 2005.

Catherine Ella Blanshard Asher was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. She completed her PhD at the University of Minnesota (~1977–1984), where she subsequently served as an Assistant Professor (~1984–2021).

Catherine Ludvik specializes in religious, Buddhist, and Japanese studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Toronto under David Waterhouse, Werner Knobl, and Antonino Forte. She taught at Stanford, Doshisha, and Kyoto Sangyo universities in 2019.

Catherine Prueitt works in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Emory University under John D. Dunne and Laurie L. Patton, later serving at George Mason University (2017–2019) and the University of British Columbia (2019).
Cathy Cantwell is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Kent in 1989 and held a post at the University of Oxford in 2002.

Cecil Bendall was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Cambridge under E. B. Cowell and Göttingen under Theodor Benfey. He held posts at the British Museum, University College London, and as Professor of Sanskrit at Cambridge.

Cecil Henry Bompas was an Indologist educated at Westminster School and Trinity College, Cambridge (1886–1889). He served in the Indian Civil Service (1887–1923), the Bengal Legislative Council (1916), and chaired the Calcutta Improvement Trust (1920).

Cecil Jermyn Brown was an Indologist and historian who earned his MA at Trinity College, Oxford. He taught at Canning College (1909–1920) and became Reader (1921) and Professor of English Literature (1923–1926) at the University of Lucknow.

Cecil Y. Lang studied at Duke University (~1937–1941). He held academic posts at the University of Chicago (~1965–1970), Yale University, and served as Professor of English at the University of Virginia (~1970–1991).
Cezary Galewicz is an Indologist based at Jagiellonian University, where he served as an Adjunct Professor (attested 2012) and became a professor in 2015.

Ch'ing-mao Cheng was a Sinologist and Japanologist. He studied at National Taiwan University and Princeton, taught at UC Berkeley, and served as Chair at the University of Massachusetts Amherst (1976–1996) and National Dong Hwa University (1996–2003).

Chack-fan Lee, active in Buddhist studies, studied at the University of Hong Kong and the University of Western Ontario. He served as Pro-Vice-Chancellor at the University of Hong Kong from 1994 to 2015.
Chaesong Kim is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Kim completed doctoral coursework at the University of Tokyo (attested 1995), studying under Yasunori Ejima.

Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers including Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Dudjom Rinpoche, Khenpo Dorje, Tromge Trungpa Rinpoche, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.

Chaim Rabin was a linguist who studied at Hebrew University, SOAS, and Oxford. He served as Cowley Lecturer in Post-Biblical Hebrew at Oxford (1943–1956) and Associate Professor at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (1956–1985).

Chaisit Suwanvarangkul works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He has served as a researcher at Kyoto University and the University of Delhi, and as Lecturer in Buddhist Studies at the University of Otago (attested 2015).

Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. After earning a doctorate in philosophy from Oxford, he held research and teaching posts at Oxford, Cambridge, NUS, and Lancaster University, where he is a Distinguished Professor.

Chamnong Adivadhanasit works in religious and Buddhist studies. A Chulalongkorn University graduate (BA), he served there as a part-time instructor and as Professor in the Faculty of Social Science at Kasetsart University (attested 2012).
